_purpose: Which workloads have run on which part, and the log that proves it.
Eleven kernel modules carried 'STATUS: UNTESTED ON HARDWARE' in their
docstrings on 2026-09-10, and every one of them had run on a
trn1.2xlarge -- some of them a fortnight earlier. A status line that
nothing checks is not a status, and in a repo whose rule is 'never
claim a kernel works without a hardware run behind it', the inverse
error matters just as much: a stale UNTESTED label makes verified
work look unverified, and leaves a reader unable to tell which of
So the record moves out of prose and into here, where
tests/test_hardware_status.py can hold the docstrings against it.
A workload is listed only if a run produced a PASS or a SKIP for it.
A FAIL is not a hardware verification -- it is evidence the kernel
reached the device, which is a different and lesser claim -- so
moe_router and transformer_train_step are recorded under the pass
that fixed them, not the one that found them.

runs.note: DURATION=10 REPEAT=3 full pass: 23 PASS, 0 FAIL. The two 2026-09-08 failures are fixed and verified here. A second pass the same day at DURATION=30 REPEAT=3 gave 24 PASS, 0 FAIL with no Score flagging itself irreproducible, and exercised the NEFF search against a warm cache for the first time: memory_read found at candidate 6 of 7, memory_write at 3 of 7, both at coverage 1.0.

--test all --duration 30 in one process: 24 PASS (baseline_metrics, which carries no Score, not listed), 0 FAIL, with the coalesced GEMM tiling as default (tensor_virus 69.56 TFLOPS, int_virus 77.18 TOPS, pulse_virus 37.42 TFLOPS) and every row-tile of each GEMM product checked. An earlier --test all the same day (trn1-full-pass-single-process.log) reported memory_read_agg and memory_write_agg as PASS at 0.0 GB/s with every worker aborted; that PASS was the defect and is not recorded as one. Here they run first and read 540.97 and 506.66 GB/s. Coalesced tiling evidence: trn1-coalesced-tiling.log; ordering before/after: trn1-aggregate-ordering.log.

never_run_anywhere.all_reduce: Needs 2+ devices for NeuronLink. Skipped on every single-device part probed. Trn quota is 64 vCPU and trn1.32xlarge needs 128, so no multi-device part has been reached.
never_run_anywhere.p2p_thrasher: Same: needs 2+ devices for a NeuronLink peer, and the same 64 vCPU Trn quota blocks every multi-device part.
